rubrics.justification: The response conflicts with the provided Gardner score 1DD by describing a visible/organized ICM, cohesive TE, thinning zona, and a good-quality expanded blastocyst; these are major fabricated or incorrect features for a 1DD embryo.

It integrates most relevant patient factors well, including age, diagnosis, endometrium, sperm, prior cycles, and lifestyle, though it overweights these positives because the embryo quality was mischaracterized.

The reasoning is internally structured but rests on a major false premise that the embryo is good quality; this leads to an implausibly optimistic prognosis and recommendations inconsistent with the stated 1DD grading.

While SET and luteal support are broadly guideline-consistent, the interpretation of Gardner grading is not aligned with standard criteria, and the implantation estimate is far too high for a 1DD embryo/day-4 poor-quality transfer.

The recommendations are practical in a general IVF sense, but they are only moderately useful because they are not tailored to the poor embryo grade and do not adequately address counseling around low expected success.
